name: Foreign Investor Residency Permit (Proposed, Not Yet Operative)

requirement_groups.name: Pending framework (approved in principle, not yet implemented)

requirements.blocker_text: On 7 February 2026, Afghanistan's Economic Commission -- chaired by Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar -- endorsed a proposal to grant foreign investors residency permits of one to ten years in exchange for capital investment, with the exact duration tied to investment volume. As of this build (7 months later), NO minimum investment threshold, no formal decree, no application procedure, and no confirmation of whether the permit could lead toward permanent residence or citizenship have been published. A separate committee was tasked with setting the volume-based duration criteria and had not reported results in any source found. This route is included because the policy has been formally approved at the executive level, but it does not yet function as an applicable process -- there is nothing to apply to.
requirements.fix_path: No application path exists yet. Monitor for the implementing committee's criteria and a formal decree before treating this as an actionable route.

evidence_required.document: Not yet defined -- no implementing regulation published

outcome.duration_length: proposed 1-10 years, tied to investment volume (unconfirmed criteria)

sources.title: IMI Daily (immigration-industry trade press) -- Economic Commission approval, 7 Feb 2026, gaps in published criteria
Ariana News (Afghan news outlet) -- confirms approving body, date, and that implementation criteria are still pending committee review
AtlasPress News Agency -- corroborates approval details and notes analyst skepticism that residency alone will attract investment given sanctions/security context

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Afghanistan). STATUS: DRAFT, AND GENUINELY NOT YET AN OPERATIVE ROUTE -- this is the Afghan analogue to Cuba's not-yet-in-force legal framework found earlier in this dataset, but even less mature: Cuba's framework was at least published as law awaiting an effective date, while Afghanistan's is a February 2026 executive-level policy approval with literally no published investment threshold, application process, or rights framework seven months later. This dataset chose to document it rather than omit it, specifically because 'approved but not yet implementable' is itself a real, current, and useful fact for anyone tracking this route. work_rights set to 'none' and study_rights omitted (not a required field) rather than guessed, since no implementing regulation exists yet to confirm either way -- 'none'/omitted here means 'not confirmed to exist,' not 'confirmed denied'; family_can_join/work set to false as the same conservative default until a framework exists to say otherwise. All three sources are tier 4 trade/local press -- no primary decree or gazette text exists yet to cite, since none has been published.
